newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends sharply up in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends sharply up in late trade.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 255 basis points at 23.80 percent on Wednesday due to what traders said was a last-minute speculative trade.

"The session was quiet with overnight government paper trading at an average of 22 percent. At the close a player who had been holding on to liquidity stepped in to take advantage of month-end demand for cash," a trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed up 60 basis points at 24 percent.
Money market analysts noted that early weakness in the peso put secondary rates under some upside pressure, but this was eased by ample market liquidity.
"The market has accumulated surplus liquidity since the end of last year. At first it was due to foreign capital inflow, and since then demand for credit has not recovered," an analyst said.
"Whereas Banco de Mexico used to inject liquidity, it has recently been draining it, something we had not seen since the end of 1994," he added.
The central bank again drained liquidty during the session, totalling 1.167 billion pesos, through two auctions to purchase paper.
Liquidity of 1.168 billion pesos is scheduled to return to the system on Thursday, added to which will be an under supply of paper for 1.628 billion pesos carried over from the primary auction.
Nonetheless, traders noted that the liquidity surplus could be reduced by month-end demand for cash. ((--Patricia
